67:AmF9t|## pi-durable extensions
68:47DEQ|
69:MI04z|A [pi-durable](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@earendil-works/pi-durable) extension adds its tools and prompt sections to every conversation: comment mode, `pr_number` runs, and direct prompts. An example is the `pit/durable` extension of [pit](https://github.com/cv/pit):
70:47DEQ|
71:j44LH|```yaml
72:JOTfh|- uses: cv/pi-action@v2
73:PI-Nw|  with:
74:TlaBm|    github_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
75:vQQQ3|    extensions: |
76:63mzr|      github:cv/pit#v0.36.3   # pit's typescript tool (pit/durable)
77:8bkBh|```
78:47DEQ|
79:wuYwZ|### Package format
80:47DEQ|
81:ouEL2|- A package is a pi-durable extension package when its `package.json` has `pi.durable`, a module path. Example: `"pi": { "durable": "./src/durable/index.ts" }`.
82:G3Arm|- The module exports `createPiDurableExtension(options)`, or a default export with the same signature.
83:67Img|- The function returns a pi-durable `Extension`: `{ name, tools?, sections?, hooks?, wraps?, tasks? }`.
84:UFwZd|- If a package has `pi.durable` and `pi.extensions`, pi-action loads only the `pi.durable` entry, because its pi extensions need the pi coding agent. pi-action writes this to the log.
85:XfjrO|- pi-action installs the extensions after its coding tools (read, write, edit, bash). Each extension must have a unique name, other than `coding-tools` and `pi-action`. Tool names can repeat (see [Override tools and sections](#override-tools-and-sections)).
86:47DEQ|
87:0tHz6|### Override tools and sections
88:47DEQ|
89:bKLT7|An extension can change the tools and prompt sections of pi-action and of other extensions:
90:47DEQ|
91:_AEgg|- **Replace a tool.** A tool with the name of an earlier tool replaces it, as `pi.registerTool` does in pi. For example, an extension with its own `bash` tool replaces the `bash` of pi-action. pi-action writes `pi-durable extension <name> replaces tool bash from coding-tools` to the log.
92:iO82-|- **Wrap a tool or a section.** `wrapTool(tool, wrapper)` and `wrapSection(key, wrapper)` of pi-durable change a tool or a section, for example its description or its text. `wrapTool("read", (t) => ({ ...t, callers: ["tools"] }))` hides `read` from the model, but other tools can still call it (see [Tools the model sees](#tools-the-model-sees)).
93:47DEQ|
94:pD3Fx|The order is: the coding tools of pi-action (`coding-tools`) first, then its built-in extension `pi-action`, then the extensions in the order of the `extensions` input. Extensions cannot use the names `coding-tools` and `pi-action`. pi-durable applies the wraps of all extensions in this order. Thus, the last wrap wins.
95:47DEQ|
96:bFqqG|The `pi-action` extension has pi's system prompt sections. Use these keys with `wrapSection`: `preamble`, `tools`, `rules`, `addendum`, `project_context`, `available_skills`, and `cwd` (see [The system prompt](prompts.md#the-system-prompt)). For example, `wrapSection("rules", (s) => ({ ...s, render: () => "- My rule" }))` replaces pi's rules.
97:47DEQ|
98:Pc3so|### Host options
99:47DEQ|
100:QilA7|`createPiDurableExtension` receives `{ cwd, agentDir, trustProject, ui, log, images }`:
101:47DEQ|
102:DkRVY|| Option | Value |
103:ZVBOk||--------|-------|
104:FdHaI|| `cwd` | The workspace |
105:zko0A|| `agentDir` | `agent_dir`, resolved against the workspace. If `agent_dir` is empty: a new temporary directory in `RUNNER_TEMP` |
106:FW0H0|| `trustProject` | The `trust_project` input |
107:cC04Q|| `ui` | `{ ask, notify }`, the GitHub UI (see [Questions on GitHub](#questions-on-github)). Only in `comment` mode on an issue or pull request. Not set in `output` mode or for direct prompts |
108:NQnrk|| `log` | The log of the action (`info`, `warning`) |
109:w2uNR|| `images` | An image processor, `createNodePhotonImages()` of pi-durable. It resizes and converts images to the limits of the model, for example for pit's `workspace.viewImage` (pit 0.36.2 and later) |
110:47DEQ|
111:rWM5q|pi-durable extensions run in the process of pi-action. Thus, pi-action also sets `GH_TOKEN` and the git identity in its own environment when it loads such an extension. See [Security](security.md#the-agents-github-token-and-git-identity).
112:47DEQ|
113:7Dwrw|### `trust_project`
114:47DEQ|
115:DnNir|`trust_project` (default `false`) tells the extension that it can load and run the configuration of the repository. For pit, this is `.pi/pit.json` and `.pi/functions`. pi-action uses it too: for the prompt templates in `.pi/prompts`, the skills in `.pi/skills` and `.agents/skills`, and `.pi/SYSTEM.md` and `.pi/APPEND_SYSTEM.md` (see [Security](security.md#skills-from-the-repository)).
116:47DEQ|
117:n6Q2s|Anyone who can push a branch or open a pull request can change those files. Set `trust_project: true` only for repositories whose code you already run. Do not set it in workflows that run on pull requests from people you do not trust.
118:47DEQ|
